Money is moving quickly into the same problem. Israeli startup Zenity Ltd. announced a $125 million round on Aug. 3 to build a security layer for AI agents, and a string of smaller rounds has gone to companies selling visibility into agentic workflows.

MaC Venture Capital Management led FriskAI’s round. Wischoff Ventures joined, along with New Enterprise Associates Inc. partner Rick Yang and a group of angel investors. Marlon Nichols, managing partner at MaC Venture Capital, likened the opportunity to what Amazon Web Services Inc. was to cloud and Cisco Systems Inc. was to the early internet and said the FriskAI team has built “the infrastructure layer that lets companies see what their agents are doing.” The company’s website also lists Detroit Venture Partners among its backers. ### FriskAI launches with $3.6M to show enterprises what their AI agents are doing

by  Duncan Riley

Runtime intelligence startup FriskAI Inc. launched today with $3.6 million in pre-seed funding to give enterprises a record of what their artificial intelligence agents actually do once they go into production.

FriskAI is aiming at a problem that comes with agents. Given different inputs, a different tool set or a shifting objective, the same agent can take a route nobody wrote down in advance. Conventional software does not improvise. The observability and security tooling most companies run was built on that assumption. [...] The pre-seed money will go toward engineering and go-to-market hiring, customer deployments and further work on the behavioral analysis side of the product. FriskAI, based in Los Angeles, is signing up users through an early access program.

# FriskAI Launches the Runtime Intelligence Platform for AI Agents, Announces $3.6 Million Pre-Seed Funding Round

 Karan Bhatia
 5 days ago
 2 min read

FriskAI, the runtime intelligence platform for AI agents, led by Neel Palrecha and the team, has announced its official launch and a $3.6 million pre-seed funding round led by MaC Venture Capital, with participation from Wischoff Ventures, NEA partner Rick Yang, and a group of strategic angel investors.

FriskAI sits between AI agents and the tools they use, capturing every action taken by an agent. [...] The platform gives organizations visibility into agent behavior, enabling teams to understand how agents operate, detect unexpected activity, investigate incidents, and deploy AI more confidently across critical workflows.

AI agents are becoming core operational infrastructure, but organizations still lack visibility into their behavior once deployed. FriskAI provides runtime intelligence for AI agents, giving companies the visibility needed to understand, monitor, and confidently deploy agents in production.

— Neel Palrecha, Founder and CEO, FriskAI

As enterprises move from deterministic software to autonomous AI agents, understanding real-world agent behavior is becoming a new operational challenge. [...] Every technology cycle creates companies that provide infrastructure others ultimately depend on, from AWS in cloud computing to Cisco during the internet boom. AI agents represent the next cycle, expanding into areas of the economy that traditional software never fully reached. Enterprise adoption at scale will depend on the ability to trust agents with critical decisions and workflows.

— Marlon Nichols, Managing Partner, MaC Venture Capital

FriskAI is building the infrastructure layer for enterprise AI agents, giving companies visibility into agent activity, security over the systems they access, and greater confidence in their outputs. Solving these challenges could make FriskAI a critical part of the enterprise AI stack.

Enterprises spent the last year handing AI agents the keys to their databases, internal tools, and customer systems. Almost none of them can tell you what those agents actually did, or what it cost them.
We led FriskAI's $3.6M pre-seed because Neel Palrecha is solving the unglamorous problem that has to get solved first: a plain, readable record of every action an agent takes, down to the tokens it burned getting there.
That second part matters more than people realize. When an agent decides its own path, spend stops being a line item you can forecast and becomes something you discover at the end of the month. Teams need to see where tokens go, which workflows are quietly expensive, and what scaling to 10x volume actually costs before they commit to it. [...] 17,258 followers

As our Managing General Partner Marlon C. Nichols shared, every major technology cycle creates foundational infrastructure companies that the rest of the ecosystem comes to depend on. We believe AI agents represent the next major cycle and trust will be essential to unlocking their potential.
